AIlegro continued joint model — runtime, provenance and training-data notice

Homepage runtime assets (browser inference only):
- vendor/lib/joint-continued-weights.js: R/H/B/M StructuredJoint backbone,
  selected from training/runs/joint-continued-expression-v1/best-base.pt,
  SHA-256 e2bde38d02d0ca957e7841b23a4d7e3502d8aaeb2ba3a8396e1bba08307c6ebd.
- vendor/lib/joint-expression-weights.js: exact-note expression sidecar,
  selected at the same step (42,377) from that run's best.pt. This predicts
  onset and duration fractions, pitch, tuplet ratio label and notated dynamics.
- vendor/lib/joint-arranger-weights.js: learned six-group note classifier,
  selected at step 202,600 from
  training/runs/joint-continued-arrangement-v1/best.pt,
  SHA-256 c1f72410dacbddd0f96547dcbbc0a363f8c54562783fb499c2386a68eefc2bbe.
  It assigns already-written notes to groups; it does not generate new voices
  and has no supervised role or Walk labels.

The previous backbone, vendor/lib/joint-weights.js, remains in the project for
historical tests and recovery but is not imported by the homepage. Its source
checkpoint is training/runs/joint-v1/structured/model.pt, SHA-256
8b269c4a6e4e4abd8ef3e2825743451da9c965155403b53a94115486fcce5059.
It originated in project-authored synthetic phrases from the earlier rule
system and OpenScore Lieder. Synthetic pop/jazz/etc conditions are not offered
in the current UI; future styles should receive separate fine-tuning.

Training data:
1. Project-authored synthetic phrases for original pretraining.
2. OpenScore Lieder, CC0 1.0 Universal, for original and continued four-track
   training and MusicXML-derived expression fields.
   Source: https://github.com/OpenScore/Lieder
   Pinned source commit: 38c5db510224d9facdc4b08d741fc788cfb58ea8
   License: https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/
   Local-key and harmony labels are bundled automatic AugmentedNet analyses.
   No audio recordings or lyrics were used.
3. The arrangement classifier also used prepared orchestral MIDI and the
   project's curated local MIDI selection. Per-file redistribution rights for
   some MIDI are unresolved. Keep local research/previews separate from any
   commercial or public model release until provenance is reviewed.

Credit OpenScore Lieder contributors and the composers/editions identified in
the source repository. The Lieder validation split selected checkpoints; test
split was not used for training/selection. Model losses and browser parity do
not establish listener preference, score quality or reliable tuplets in every
generated passage. MIDI velocity is not a notated dynamic mark.
